docs.title: Built-in Interactive Guided Tutorials ([↰] [C] / [↰] [?])
docs.text:
Every calculator in the StackCalc Domain Series includes an on-device interactive tutor engine, launched by pressing [↰] [C] (yellow-shifted [↰] [?]). The runner observes keypresses in real-time, coaching the user step-by-step through foundational RPN mechanics and flagship domain calculations:

Instrument Built-in Lesson 1 Built-in Lesson 2 Built-in Lesson 3 SC-35 RPN Primer: Distance and bearing coordinate product Field Aviation: Crosswind component and heading correction Spirit Leveling: Benchmark elevation and differential rod transfer ([f] [LVL]) SC-14 RPN Primer: Single-phase real power (\(P = V \times I\)) Roof Framing: Rafter run, rise, and hypotenuse geometry Voltage Drop: NEC conductor series drop along long feeders ([AWG]) SC-16 RPN Primer: Hexadecimal address offset accumulation CIDR Bitwise: Netmask synthesis and usable host capacity Bitwise Logic: Multi-byte bitwise AND masking (0xDEAD AND 0xBEEF) SC-24 RPN Primer: Frame count accumulation (\(24\text{ fps} \times 5\text{ s}\)) Audio Exposure: Base-2 EV balance and rotary shutter angle Photometrics: Inverse-square illuminance and falloff ([LUX]) SC-50 RPN Primer: Transmitter power and antenna gain summation RF Physics: Dipole physical resonance and quarter-wave length Path Loss: Friis free-space microwave link loss ([FSL]) SC-60 RPN Primer: Reagent molar mass to gram conversion Lab Molarity: Solution concentration and primary standards Buffer pH: Henderson–Hasselbalch conjugate equilibrium ([BUF]) SC-78 RPN Primer: Sourdough flour and hydration mass sum Brewing ABV: Hydrometer extract drop and alcohol yield Water Temp: Four-term Desired Dough Temperature balance ([Tw]) SC-80 RPN Primer: Unit dose to total daily administration Pediatric Dosing: Body weight-based milligram calculation Vasoactive Drip: Critical microgram infusion rate ([DRP]) SC-95 RPN Primer: Gross revenue minus expense operating profit Margin & Markup: Selling price versus cost percentage Gaussian CDF: Standard normal cumulative probability tail ([g] [pN])

docs.title: Dynamic Live Reference Ledgers ([g] [▦])
docs.text:
Pressing [g] [▦] ([↱] [+/-]) opens the non-destructive domain reference ledger. Unlike a static table of physical constants, the StackCalc ledger dynamically tracks data accumulated in real time with [f] [PT+] or [Σ+]:

  • SC-35 (@COGO): Accumulates polygon perimeter coordinates, calculates cumulative linear misclosure (CLOS), and computes Gauss's Shoelace polygon area (AREA) in square feet, acres, and hectares.
  • SC-14 (@BOM / Service Sizing): Sums individual branch circuit loads via [Σ+], calculates total load (TOT LOAD), applies the NEC 125% continuous duty multiplier (80% CONT), and automatically selects the minimum standard service panel rating (PNL MIN: 100A, 125A, 200A, 400A).
  • SC-16 (Registers & Cyber): Decomposes the active register into simultaneous HEX, DEC, OCT, and BIN representations, extracts IEEE-754 32/64-bit sign, exponent, and mantissa bitfields, formats fixed-point Q16.16, and calculates 4-byte and 8-byte struct alignment padding (ALIGN 4B, ALIGN 8B).
  • SC-24 (Cinema Production Log): Logs scene takes with [Σ+], tracking total accumulated timecode (TOTAL TC), total frames (TOTAL F), take count (TAKES), average take duration (AVG TAKE), camera raw data generated (DATA GEN in GB), and remaining card recording runtime (512G REM in hours).
  • SC-50 (Smith & Friis Cascade): Evaluates complex reflection parameters (|GAMMA|, GAMMA ANG, VSWR, RET LOSS, normalized \(r/z_0\) and \(x/z_0\)), and sums multi-stage RF amplifiers via [Σ+] to compute total cascaded gain (CASC G) and Friis cascaded noise figure (CASC NF).
  • SC-60 (Solution & Formula Mass Breakdown): Accumulates gravimetric solute masses via [Σ+] to display solute mass percent (SOL1 %, TOT MASS), and parses active chemical formulas (FML, MW) into live per-element mass percentage breakdowns (H MASS%, O MASS%, etc.).
  • SC-78 (Baking Formula Ledger): Anchors formula flour weight (FLOUR), computes live Baker's percentages for all added ingredients (ING1 %, ING2 %), and tracks total batch dough weight (TOT W).
  • SC-80 (Patient Clinical Dashboard): Displays the persistent Patient Profile: patient weight (PAT WT), height (PAT HT), age and sex (PAT AGE), serum creatinine (PAT SCR), Mosteller Body Surface Area (PAT BSA), Devine Ideal Body Weight (PAT IBW), and Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance (PAT GFR).
  • SC-95 (Bivariate Statistics & Regression): Accumulates \((x, y)\) sample points via [Σ+], tracking sample count (\(n\)), means (\(\bar{x}, \bar{y}\)), standard deviations (\(s_x, s_y\)), ordinary least-squares slope (\(m\)), intercept (\(b\)), Pearson correlation (\(r\)), coefficient of determination (\(r^2\)), and the last 10 points.

docs.title: Geomatics, Land Surveying, and Flight Navigation Keycaps
docs.text:
On the SC-35 the Row 1 and Row 2 geomatics keys and shifted trigonometric/navigation operators execute plane coordinate geometry (COGO), horizontal and vertical highway curves, Bowditch traverse closure, sexagesimal angle conversions, and E6B aviation wind-triangle and density-altitude solutions:

Keycap / Softkey Layer Operation & Stack Signature [TRV] / [f] [PT+] Row 1 Col 0 Primary / Row 2 Col 0 Yellow Forward Traverse & Station Accumulator: Consumes distance \(D\) and azimuth \(\alpha\) to resolve \((\Delta N, \Delta E)\) ([f] [N⇄E] swaps Northing/Easting), and [f] [PT+] accumulates station coordinates into @COGO. [INV] / [g] [CLS] Row 1 Col 1 Primary / Blue Shift Coordinate Inverse & Bowditch Closure: Consumes \(\Delta N\) (\(Y\)) and \(\Delta E\) (\(X\)) to return azimuth \(\alpha\) and distance \(D\); [g] [CLS] computes traverse closure error and precision ratio. [BRG] / [f] [N⇄E] Row 1 Col 2 Primary / Yellow Shift Quadrant Bearing & Axis Swap: Formats azimuth in \(X\) as surveyor quadrant bearing (NE, SE, SW, NW), and [f] [N⇄E] swaps active Northing/Easting coordinates. [f] [ISC] Row 4 Col 1 Yellow Shift ([7]) Bearing-Bearing Intersection Workspace ([f] [ISC]): Solves N = (N1·T2 - N2·T1 + ΔE) / ΔT ([N], [D], [A]) or solves directly on the stack with bearings in \(Y\) and \(X\). [CRV] / [g] [STA] Row 1 Col 3 Primary / Row 2 Col 1 Blue Horizontal Curve Workspace ([CRV]) & Stationing: Solves circular arc L = R × D × π / 180 ([L], [R], [D]) and formats highway stationing XX+XX.XX. [SLP] / [f] [VCV] / [g] [GR%] Row 1 Col 4 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Slope Reduction, Vertical Curve & Grade %: Reduces slope distance/angle ([SLP]), solves parabolic vertical curves ([f] [VCV]), and computes percent grade ([g] [GR%]). [f] [LVL] / [FLW] / [g] [CUT] Row 1 Col 1 Yellow / Row 1 Col 5 Primary / Row 7 Col 1 Blue Differential Leveling ([f] [LVL]), Open-Channel Flow ([FLW]) & Earthwork Cut/Fill ([g] [CUT]): Solves E = H + B - F ([E], [H], [B], [F]), continuity Q = A × V, and cut/fill volumes ([g] [CUT]), while triangle geometry is evaluated via [g] [EQN] TRI. [f] [WND] / [g] [XWC] Row 5 Col 2 (Yellow / Blue Shift) E6B Wind Triangle Workspace ([f] [WND]) & Crosswind: Solves X = V × SIN(A) ([X], [V], [A]) or evaluates crosswind/headwind components on the stack ([g] [XWC]). [▸HR] / [f] [▸HMS] / [g] [ALT] Row 7 Col 3 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Sexagesimal Conversions & Density Altitude ([g] [ALT]): Converts DDD.MMSS to decimal degrees/hours ([▸HR]) and back ([f] [▸HMS]), and solves density altitude D = P + 120 × (T - 15) ([D], [P], [T]). [TSD] / [f] [DALT] / [g] [TID] Row 2 Col 2 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Time-Speed-Distance ([TSD]), Density Altitude ([f] [DALT]) & Tidal Height ([g] [TID]): Solves D = S × T ([D], [S], [T]), evaluates density altitude ([f] [DALT]), and computes rule-of-twelfths tidal stage ([g] [TID]), while weight and balance is solved via [g] [EQN] CG. [▸HR] / [f] [▸HMS] / [f] [▸DEG] / [g] [▸RAD] / [g] [▸GRD] Angular & Sexagesimal Shifts Converts packed sexagesimal DDD.MMSS to decimal degrees/hours ([▸HR]) and back ([f] [▸HMS]), or converts between degrees, radians, and gradians. [f] [▸θ,r] / [g] [▸y,x] / [f] [f-i] Coordinate & Feet-Inch Shifts Converts between Rectangular \((Y, X)\) and Polar \((r, \theta)\) coordinates and enters/formats feet-inch-fractions ([f] [f-i]).

docs.title: Industrial Trades, Electrical, and Mechanical Keycaps
docs.text:
On the SC-14 the Row 1 and Row 2 electrical, conduit, piping, and machining keys pair with dimensional shift converters to resolve National Electrical Code (NEC) conductor sizing, three-phase power and motor full-load amps, conduit offset bends, industrial process flow, and spindle machining speeds:

Keycap / Softkey Layer Operation & Stack Signature [AWG] / [f] [VDRP] / [g] [FLA] Row 1 Col 1 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) NEC Conductor Sizing ([AWG]), Voltage Drop ([f] [VDRP]) & Full-Load Amps ([g] [FLA]): Looks up NEC Table 8 conductor resistance \(R\) (\(\Omega/\text{kft}\)) and solves feeder voltage drop ([f] [VDRP]), conductor sizing, and three-phase full-load current ([g] [FLA]), while motor horsepower is solved via [g] [EQN] MTR. [OFS] / [f] [MIT] / [g] [FIT] Row 1 Col 2 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Conduit Offset ([OFS]), Miter Angle & Pipe Fitting Take-Off: Solves T = O / SIN(A) ([T], [O], [A]) on the stack or bidirectionally, miter cut angle ([f] [MIT]), and elbow fitting take-off ([g] [FIT]). [PF] / [f] [Ω] / [g] [kVA] / [x∥y] Electrical Power & Impedance Keys Power Factor ([PF]), Ohm's Law ([XEQ]), Transformer ([XEQ]) & Parallel ([x∥y]): Solves real power P = V × I × F ([P], [V], [I], [F]), P = V × I, three-phase S = V × I × 1.732 / 1000, and parallel impedance \(X \parallel Y = XY/(X+Y)\). [XL] / [f] [XC] / [g] [S] Row 1 Col 4 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) AC Reactance & Apparent Power ([XL], [f] [XC], [g] [S]): Evaluates inductive reactance \(X_L = 2\pi f L\) ([XL]), capacitive reactance \(X_C = 1/(2\pi f C)\) ([f] [XC]), and apparent AC power \(S = V \times I\) ([g] [S]), while piping continuity is evaluated via [g] [EQN] PIP. [g] [Cᵥ] / [g] [NPH] / [f] [Isc] / [g] [CFM] / [f] [SLNG] Process & Mechanical Flow Keys Valve \(C_v\) ([g] [Cᵥ]), NPSH ([g] [NPH]), Short-Circuit Current ([f] [Isc]), Airflow CFM & Rigging Sling: Solves valve flow coefficient Q = C × √(P / G) ([g] [Cᵥ]), net positive suction head ([g] [NPH]), transformer available short-circuit current ([f] [Isc]), HVAC airflow CFM ([g] [CFM]), and rigging sling angle tension multiplier ([f] [SLNG]), while pump power is solved via [g] [EQN] PMP. [mA] / [f] [RTD] / [g] [STM] Row 2 Col 2 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) 4–20 mA Loop Scaling, Callendar–Van Dusen RTD & Saturated Steam: Converts between \(4\text{--}20\text{ mA}\) current and engineering span ([mA]), Pt100 RTD resistance/temperature ([f] [RTD]), and steam pressure/temperature ([g] [STM]). [f] [SFM] / [g] [WLD] / [f] [TAP] / [g] [RPM] / [g] [BC] Machining, Welding & Millwright Keys Surface Speed ([f] [SFM]), Weld Heat ([g] [WLD]), Tap Drill, Belt Ratio & Bolt Circle ([g] [BC]): Solves spindle speed N = 3.82 × S / D ([N], [S], [D]), weld heat input H = 60 × V × I / (1000 × S) ([H], [V], [I], [S]), tap drill allowance ([f] [TAP]), pulley ratio ([g] [RPM]), and bolt-circle chord C = D × SIN(180 / N) ([C], [D], [N]). [f] [f-i] / [g] [▸mm] / [g] [▸in] / [f] [▸cm] / [f] [▸kW] / [g] [▸HP] / [f] [▸PSI] / [g] [▸kPa] / [f] [▸Nm] / [g] [▸lbf] / [f] [▸GPM] / [g] [▸MGD] Dimensional & Trade Converters Enters/formats feet-inch-fractions ([f] [f-i]) and converts between metric and US customary length, power, pressure, torque, and flow units.

docs.title: Systems Programming, Embedded, and Cyber Operations Keycaps
docs.text:
On the SC-16 radix and word-architecture keys pair with bitwise logical operators, bit shifts, circular rotations, embedded timer/ADC workspaces, and modular/network keys (while Row 0 softkeys automatically become hexadecimal digits [A]–[F] whenever [HEX] mode is active):

Keycap / Softkey Layer Operation & Stack Signature [HEX] / [f] [DEC] / [f] [OCT] / [g] [BIN] Row 1 Col 1 & Col 5 Switches display and keypad entry across base-16 hexadecimal (binding softkeys to [A]–[F]), base-10 decimal, base-8 octal, and base-2 binary view. [g] [WSZ] / [g] [UNS] / [f] [NEG] / [g] [OVF] Word Architecture & Sign Keys Cycles hardware word width across 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit registers ([g] [WSZ]), toggles unsigned interpretation ([g] [UNS]), applies two's complement negation \(-X \equiv \sim X + 1 \pmod{2^W}\) ([f] [NEG]), and inspects carry/overflow status ([g] [OVF]). [FLT] / [f] [F16] / [g] [F64] / [f] [Q.n] / [g] [FXP] Row 1 Col 2 & Row 7 Col 2 Encodes/decodes IEEE 754 float32 ([FLT]), float16 ([f] [F16]), and float64 ([g] [F64]) bit patterns, and converts real coefficients to/from \(Q_{m.n}\) fixed-point integers ([f] [Q.n], [g] [FXP]). [&] / [f] [~&] / [g] [~] / [ ] / [f] [~ ] / [⊕] [≪] / [≫] / [f] [ASR] / [g] [ROR] Row 1 Cols 3–4 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Logical shift left ([≪], \(Y \ll X\)), logical shift right ([≫], \(Y \ggg X\)), sign-preserving arithmetic shift right ([f] [ASR], \(Y \gg X\)), and circular bit rotation ([g] [ROR]). [f] [SB] / [f] [CB] / [g] [B?] / [f] [MSK] Bitfield Manipulation Keys Sets ([f] [SB]), clears ([f] [CB]), or tests ([g] [B?]) bit index \(X\) in word \(Y\), or generates a contiguous \(X\)-bit mask \(2^X - 1\) ([f] [MSK]). [f] [#B] / [g] [CLZ] / [g] [2ˣ] / [lg] Bit Counting & Base-2 Keys Counts set 1-bits (Hamming weight [f] [#B]) or leading zeros ([g] [CLZ]) in \(X\), and evaluates exact base-2 powers \(2^X\) ([g] [2ˣ]) and \(\log_2(X)\) ([lg]). [g] [PWM] / [f] [τ] / [g] [ALN] / [g] [BPS] Row 4 Col 4, Row 3 Col 4 & Row 2 Col 1 Timer ([g] [PWM]), RC Settling ([f] [τ]), Memory Alignment & UART Baud: Solves F = C / (P × A) ([F], [C], [P], [A]), RC time constant T = R × C ([T], [R], [C]), power-of-two address alignment ([g] [ALN]), and UART baud divisor ([g] [BPS]). [f] [ADC] / [g] [DAC] Mixed-Signal Keys ADC Quantization Workspace ([f] [ADC]) & DAC Output: Solves D = (V / R) × 2^N ([D], [V], [R], [N]) and reconstructs analog DAC output voltage ([g] [DAC]). [MOD] / [f] [÷R] / [g] [WSZ] / [NET] / [f] [CRC] / [g] [SWP] Row 7 Col 3 & Networking/Data Keys Evaluates remainder \(Y \bmod X\) ([MOD]), integer quotient ([f] [÷R]), word size cycle ([g] [WSZ]), IPv4 [NET] host capacity, IEEE 802.3 CRC-32 ([f] [CRC]), and endian swap ([g] [SWP]). [f] [▸B] / [g] [▸bit] / [f] [▸KiB] / [g] [▸MiB] / [f] [▸GiB] / [g] [▸TiB] / [f] [▸ms] / [g] [▸μs] / [f] [▸cyc] / [g] [▸ns] Storage & Clock Converters Converts between IEC binary storage prefixes (\(2^{10}\)–\(2^{40}\)), bytes/bits (\(\times 8\)), and clock cycle period ([f] [▸cyc], [g] [▸ns], [g] [▸μs], [f] [▸ms]).

docs.title: Cinema Optics, Broadcast Timecode, and Sound Keycaps
docs.text:
On the SC-24 the Row 1 and Row 2 camera, lighting, audio, and DIT keys pair with Row 7 SMPTE timecode solvers to evaluate angle of view, rotary shutter exposure, hyperfocal and depth-of-field lens geometry, mired color-temperature shifts, and location sound acoustics:

Keycap / Softkey Layer Operation & Stack Signature [FOV] / [f] [▸35] / [g] [▸16] / [g] [a:b] Optics & Format Keys Angle of View ([FOV]), Crop Factors & Aspect Ratio: Solves A = 2 × ATAN(W / (2 × F)) ([A], [W], [F]), applies Super-35 ([f] [▸35]) and 16mm ([g] [▸16]) crop equivalents, and evaluates frame aspect ratio ([g] [a:b]). [EV] / [f] [SHT] / [g] [GEL] Row 1 Col 1 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Exposure Value ([EV]), Rotary Shutter & CTO/CTB Gel Mired Shift: Solves N² = T × 2^E ([N], [T], [E]), shutter exposure time \(t = \theta_{\text{shutter}} / (360 \cdot \text{FPS})\) ([f] [SHT]), and mired color shift \(10^6/T_2 - 10^6/T_1\) ([g] [GEL]). [LUX] / [f] [BM°] / [f] [▸fc] / [g] [▸lux] / [f] [▸MRD] / [g] [▸K] Photometrics & Color Keys Inverse-Square Illuminance ([LUX]), Beam Spread & Photometric Units: Solves E = I / D² ([E], [I], [D]), luminaire beam diameter ([f] [BM°]), footcandles/lux ([f] [▸fc], [g] [▸lux]), and mired/Kelvin conversions ([f] [▸MRD], [g] [▸K]). [DOF] / [f] [HFD] / [g] [BPM] / [g] [▸EV] / [g] [▸ND] Depth of Field, Audio & Filter Keys Depth of Field ([DOF]), Hyperfocal, Music BPM & ND Stops: Solves H = F² / (N × C) ([H], [F], [N], [C]), direct hyperfocal distance ([f] [HFD]), music beats per minute tempo sync ([g] [BPM]), and optical density / EV stops ([g] [▸EV], [g] [▸ND]). [dB] / [f] [SPL] / [g] [λ] / [f] [vₛ] / [g] [DLY] / [g] [SYN] Acoustic & Audio Keys Evaluates decibel voltage/power ratios ([dB]), inverse-square SPL attenuation ([f] [SPL]), acoustic wavelength ([g] [λ]) using speed of sound [f] [vₛ], delay tower alignment ([g] [DLY]), and audio-video lip-sync offset ([g] [SYN]). [BIT] / [f] [TB] / [g] [W/A] / [g] [λ] DIT Data & Gaffer Power Keys Uncompressed Data Rate ([BIT]), RAID Capacity, Stage Power & Wavelength: Solves R = B × F / 8 ([R], [B], [F]), storage footprint ([f] [TB]), stage tie-in electrical load ([g] [W/A]), and optical/acoustic wavelength ([g] [λ]). [FPS] / [f] [DF] / [g] [+TC] / [g] [-TC] / [f] [▸FRM] / [g] [▸TC] Timecode & Frame-Rate Keys SMPTE Timecode & Frame Arithmetic: Solves F = S × R (via [g] [EQN] TC), sets frame rate ([FPS]), computes SMPTE 29.97 drop-frame drift ([f] [DF]), adds/subtracts timecode ([g] [+TC], [g] [-TC]), and converts between frames and HH:MM:SS:FF ([f] [▸FRM], [g] [▸TC]).

docs.title: RF Spectrum, Transmission Lines, and Microwave Keycaps
docs.text:
On the SC-50 the Row 1 and Row 2 RF propagation, impedance matching, and dynamic range keys pair with bidirectional Equation Workspaces and decibel converters to solve transmission-line standing waves, resonant LC networks, free-space link budgets, cascaded noise figures, Shannon capacity, and radar Doppler shifts:

Keycap / Softkey Layer Operation & Stack Signature [dBm] / [f] [▸dBm] / [g] [▸mW] / [f] [▸dBW] / [g] [▸W] / [f] [▸dB] / [g] [▸Lin] Power & Ratio Decibel Keys Converts linear power in milliwatts to \(\text{dBm}\) ([dBm], [f] [▸dBm]), milliwatts ([g] [▸mW]), Watts and \(\text{dBW}\) ([g] [▸W], [f] [▸dBW]), and general decibel to/from linear power ratios ([f] [▸dB], [g] [▸Lin]). [SWR] / [Γ] / [g] [TLN] / [g] [COX] Impedance & Transmission-Line Keys Standing Wave ([SWR]) & Quarter-Wave ([g] [Z₀]) Workspaces: Solves S = (1 + G) / (1 - G) ([S], [G]) and quarter-wave transformer Z = √(S × L) ([Z], [S], [L]), transmission-line electrical length ([g] [TLN]), and coaxial attenuation ([g] [COX]). [FSL] / [f] [LNK] / [g] [F₁] / [f] [λ/L] Propagation & Antenna Keys Friis Path Loss ([FSL]), Link Budget ([f] [LNK]), Fresnel Zone & Whip Length: Solves L = 20LOG(D) + 20LOG(F) + 32.44 ([L], [D], [F]), link budget R = P + G - L ([R], [P], [G], [L]), first Fresnel zone radius ([g] [F₁]), and quarter-wave whip length ([f] [λ/L]). [NF] / [f] [IP3] / [g] [FDR] / [g] [Pₙ] / [g] [dBc] Receiver Noise & Dynamic Range Friis Cascaded Noise ([NF]), Cascaded IIP3, SFDR & Thermal Floor: Solves F = A + (B - 1) / G ([F], [A], [B], [G]), cascaded third-order intercept ([f] [IP3]), spurious-free dynamic range ([g] [FDR]), thermal noise floor \(P_n = -174 + 10\log_{10}(B)\) ([g] [Pₙ]), and oscillator phase noise ([g] [dBc]). [f] [f₀] / [f] [XLC] / [f] [PAD] / [g] [fc] / [g] [EIA] Resonance, Reactance & Filter Keys LC Tank ([f] [f₀]), Reactance, Attenuator Pad & Cutoff: Solves F = 1 / (2π√(L×C)) ([F], [L], [C]), inductive/capacitive reactance ([f] [XLC]), resistive \(\pi\)/\(T\)-pad resistors ([f] [PAD]), RC/RL \(-3\text{ dB}\) cutoff ([g] [fc]), and EIA SMD codes ([g] [EIA]). [g] [C/B] / [f] [RCS] / [g] [Δf] Spectrum & Radar Solvers Shannon Capacity ([g] [C/B]), Radar Range & Doppler Shift: Solves C = B × LN(1 + S) / LN(2) ([C], [B], [S]), monostatic radar range/RCS ([f] [RCS]), and two-way radar Doppler shift \(\Delta f = 2 v f_0 / c\) ([g] [Δf]). [g] [Z₀] / [g] [T₀] / [g] [c] / [f] [kB] RF Reference Constants Recalls or configures characteristic system impedance \(Z_0\) (\(50\,\Omega\)), IEEE reference noise temperature \(T_0\) (\(290\text{ K}\)), speed of light \(c\), and Boltzmann constant \(k_B\).

docs.title: Wet-Lab Chemistry, Stoichiometry, and Spectroscopy Keycaps
docs.text:
On the SC-60 the Row 1 and Row 2 analytical chemistry keys and bidirectional Equation Workspaces evaluate formula molecular weights, gravimetric molarity, stock aliquot dilutions, Sørensen \(\text{pH}\), Henderson–Hasselbalch buffer pairs, Beer–Lambert optical absorbance, chemical thermodynamics, and Nernstian electrochemistry:

Keycap / Softkey Layer Operation & Stack Signature [Z] / [MW] / [f] [w/w] / [f] [ION] Atomic & Gravimetric Keys Element Lookup (Z), Molar Mass ([MW]) & Mass Fraction: Recalls 118-element IUPAC atomic mass ([Z] with \(X > 0\)) or opens Formula Mode ([Z] with \(X = 0\); softkeys [ALP], [NUM], [FML]), solves W = N × M ([W], [N], [M]), mass percent ([f] [w/w]), and polyatomic ion ledger ([f] [ION]). [C₁V₁] / [f] [RXN] / [g] [w/v] Row 2 Col 2 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Dilution ([C₁V₁]), Stoichiometry ([f] [RXN]) & Weight/Volume %: Solves C × V = D × U ([C], [V], [D], [U]), molar stoichiometry N = C × V ([N], [C], [V]), and \(\%(\text{w/v})\) concentration ([g] [w/v]). [εbc] / [f] [CLAU] Row 2 Col 3 (Primary / Yellow) Beer–Lambert ([εbc]) & Clausius–Clapeyron ([f] [CLAU]): Solves A = E × B × C ([A], [E], [B], [C]) and vapor pressure equilibrium via the Clausius–Clapeyron relation ([f] [CLAU]). [g] [pH] / [f] [EQV] / [g] [PVT] Row 2 Col 4 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Sørensen pH, Titration ([f] [EQV]) & Ideal Gas Workspace ([g] [PVT]): Converts \([\text{H}^+]\) to \(\text{pH} = -\log_{10}(X)\) ([g] [pH]), solves titration equivalence A × V = B × U, and ideal gas law P × V = N × 8.3145 × T ([P], [V], [N], [T]). [BUF] / [f] [%Y] / [g] [CAL] Row 2 Col 5 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Henderson–Hasselbalch Buffer ([BUF]), Yield & Calorimetry ([g] [CAL]): Solves buffer P = K + LOG(A / H) ([P], [K], [A], [H]), percent yield ([f] [%Y]), and heat transfer Q = M × C × T ([Q], [M], [C], [T]). [%] / [f] [Δ%] / [f] [▸M] / [g] [▸g/L] Concentrations & Percentages Evaluates percentages ([%], [f] [Δ%]) and molarity/mass concentration conversions ([f] [▸M], [g] [▸g/L]), while centrifuge RCF is evaluated with the canonical stack sequence. [g] [Kₑq] / [g] [Eₐ] / [f] [ΔG] / [g] [E°] Kinetics & Thermodynamics Keys Arrhenius Kinetics Workspace ([g] [Eₐ]), Equilibrium & Electrochemistry: Solves K = A × EXP(-E / (R × T)) ([K], [A], [E], [T]), equilibrium constant ([g] [Kₑq]), Gibbs free energy G = H - T × S ([f] [ΔG]), and standard potential E = S - (0.05916/N)LOG(Q) ([g] [E°]). [g] [R] / [g] [h] / [f] [kB] / [g] [c] Fundamental Physical Constants Recalls CODATA molar gas constant \(R\), Planck constant \(h\), Boltzmann constant \(k_B\), and speed of light \(c\).

docs.title: Commercial Bakery, Fermentation Science, and Brewing Keycaps
docs.text:
On the SC-78 the Row 1 bakery and culinary yield keys and Row 2 brewing and enology keys pair with bidirectional Equation Workspaces to anchor batch scaling to total flour mass, compute mix water and flake-ice mass from friction and ambient heat, evaluate brewing gravity attenuation, strike water temperature, and hop bitterness, and audit butcher trim yields and menu food cost:

Keycap / Softkey Layer Operation & Stack Signature [BK%] / [g] [HYD] / [f] [SCL] / [PAN] Baker's Percentage & Scaling Keys Baker's % ([BK%]), Hydration, Batch Scale & Pan Scaling: Consumes flour mass (\(Y\)) and ingredient mass (\(X\)) or opens P = (I / F) × 100 ([P], [I], [F]), computes dough hydration % ([g] [HYD]), scales ingredient weights ([f] [SCL]), and scales across pan volumes ([PAN]). [LEV] / [f] [PRF] / [g] [LV%] Row 1 Col 1 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Sourdough Starter ([LEV]), Proofing Time & inoculation ([g] [LV%]): Splits levain build mass into flour/water components ([LEV]), adjusts fermentation proof time for ambient temperature \(Q_{10}\) ([f] [PRF]), and computes pre-ferment inoculation % ([g] [LV%]). [Tw] / [ΣW] / [f] [DIV] / [g] [ΔHf] Row 1 Cols 3–4 & Row 3 Col 5 Blue Desired Dough Temp ([Tw]), Total Weight, Portion Divide & Flake Ice: Solves W = 3 × D - R - F - M ([W], [D], [R], [F], [M]), computes total dough mass from flour and total baker's % ([ΣW]), divides batch into equal loaves ([f] [DIV]), and recalls ice latent heat of fusion ([g] [ΔHf]) for water cooling calculations. [ABV] / [f] [CHP] / [g] [SRM] / [f] [BRX] / [g] [SGT] Gravity, Alcohol & Color Keys Alcohol by Volume ([ABV]), Chaptalization, Morey SRM & Hydrometer: Solves A = (O - F) × 131.25 ([A], [O], [F]), sugar addition ([f] [CHP]), beer color \(\text{SRM} = 1.4922 \cdot \text{MCU}^{0.6859}\) ([g] [SRM]), alcohol-corrected refractometer FG ([f] [BRX]), and hydrometer temperature correction ([g] [SGT]). [MSH] / [f] [SPG] / [g] [PU] Row 2 Col 4 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Mash Strike ([MSH]), Sparge Volume & Pasteurization ([g] [PU]): Solves S = (0.2 / R) × (T - G) + T ([S], [R], [T], [G]), boil/sparge volume ([f] [SPG]), and thermal pasteurization units ([g] [PU]). [IBU] / [f] [BLOM] / [g] [PRC] Row 2 Col 5 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Hop Bitterness ([IBU]), Bloom Strength & Menu Price ([g] [PRC]): Solves I = W × A × U × 74.89 / V ([I], [W], [A], [U], [V]), gelatin bloom gel strength adjustment ([f] [BLOM]), and menu pricing from food cost % ([g] [PRC]). [C₁V₁] / [f] [MSO2] / [g] [EXT%] / [f] [ACD] / [g] [SYR] Enology, Extraction & Acid Keys Solves Pearson dilution C × V = D × U ([C₁V₁]), molecular free \(\text{SO}_2\) preservation ([f] [MSO2]), mash extraction efficiency ([g] [EXT%]), acid blend adjustment ([f] [ACD]), and confectionery syrup boiling point elevation ([g] [SYR]). [F0] / [f] [MAC] / [g] [CST] / [%] / [f] [Δ%] / [g] [a:b] Row 1 Col 5 & Row 7 Col 3 Thermal Lethality ([F0]), Plate Costing ([g] [CST]) & Ratios: Computes commercial sterilization \(F_0\) value ([F0]), Atwater caloric macros ([f] [MAC]), solves menu plate costing P = C / (F / 100) ([P], [C], [F]), percentages, and hydration ratios ([g] [a:b]). [f] [▸Brx] / [g] [▸SG] / [f] [▸°P] / [g] [▸PRF] / [g] [TDS] / [f] [DTR] / [f] [SAL] / [g] [SV] / [g] [SYR] / [g] [Aw] Culinary R&D & Sugar Scale Keys Converts between Brix, Specific Gravity, Plato, and US Proof; evaluates coffee extraction yield ([g] [TDS]) and roast development time ratio ([f] [DTR]), equilibrium brine salinity ([f] [SAL]), sous-vide thermal diffusion ([g] [SV]), syrup Brix ([g] [SYR]), and water activity ([g] [Aw]).

docs.title: Clinical Nursing, Hospital Pharmacy, and Infusions Keycaps
docs.text:
On the SC-80 the Row 1 and Row 2 clinical dosing, clearance, and pharmacy compounding keys pair with the Patient Profile softkey bar ([PAT]: [W], [H], [A], [S], [MALE]/[FEM]) to evaluate Mosteller body surface area, Devine ideal and adjusted dosing weights, Cockcroft–Gault renal clearance, pediatric maintenance rules, vasoactive pump and gravity drip rates, and one-compartment pharmacokinetics:

Keycap / Softkey Layer Operation & Stack Signature [BSA] / [f] [IBW] / [g] [ABW] / [g] [BMI] Anthropometric & Dosing Weight Keys Mosteller BSA ([BSA]), Ideal/Adjusted Weight & BMI: Consumes height in \(\text{cm}\) (\(Y\)) and weight in \(\text{kg}\) (\(X\)) or solves B = √(H × W / 3600) ([B], [H], [W], [PAT]), Devine ideal body weight ([f] [IBW]), \(40\%\) obese-adjusted dosing weight ([g] [ABW]), and Quetelet BMI ([g] [BMI]). [GFR] / [PAT] Row 1 Col 2 & Patient Softkey Cockcroft–Gault Renal Clearance ([GFR]): Solves C = ((140 - A) × W) / (72 × S) ([C], [A], [W], [S], [PAT]), automatically applying the \(\times 0.85\) female sex factor when [FEM] is active in the [PAT] profile. [DRP] / [IV] / [gtt] / [EOSM] / [g] [MGH] Critical-Care Infusion & Titration Keys Vasoactive Drip ([DRP]), Volumetric Pump ([IV]), Gravity (gtt) & Osmolality ([EOSM]): Solves R = D × W × 60 / C ([R], [D], [W], [C], [PAT]), pump rate R = V / T ([R], [V], [T]), gravity drip rate ([gtt]), effective serum osmolality ([EOSM]), and \(\text{mg/hr}\) mass rate ([g] [MGH]), while weight-based dose is evaluated via [g] [EQN] DOS. [f] [FWD] / [f] [ALG] / [g] [IST] / [f] [VIL] / [f] [GIR] Pharmacy Compounding & Fluids Evaluates free water deficit ([f] [FWD]), two-stock alligation alternate ratio ([f] [ALG]), sodium chloride isotonicity equivalent ([g] [IST]), powder vial reconstitution volume ([f] [VIL]), and neonatal glucose infusion rate ([f] [GIR]). [f] [PED] / [g] [421] / [f] [REE] / [g] [VET] Pediatric, Metabolic & Veterinary Keys Computes Clark/Young pediatric dose ([f] [PED]), Holliday–Segar 4-2-1 hourly maintenance fluid rate ([g] [421]), Mifflin–St Jeor resting energy expenditure ([f] [REE]), and Kleiber allometric veterinary metabolic energy \(70 \cdot W_{\text{kg}}^{0.75}\) ([g] [VET]). [PK] / [g] [PCO2] / [g] [FENa] Pharmacokinetics & Renal Solvers One-Compartment Elimination ([PK]), Expected \(P\text{CO}_2\) & FENa: Converts between \(k_e\) and \(t_{1/2} = \ln(2)/k_e\) on the stack or solves T = 0.693 × V / C ([T], [V], [C]), calculates Winter's expected \(P\text{CO}_2\) ([g] [PCO2]), and solves fractional excretion of sodium ([g] [FENa]). [g] [Na⁺] / [EOSM] / [A-a] / [g] [PCO2] Serum Electrolyte & Respiratory Keys Evaluates Katz hyperglycemia-corrected sodium ([g] [Na⁺]), effective serum osmolality ([EOSM]), alveolar-arterial oxygen gradient \(A\text{-}a\) ([A-a]), and Winter's formula expected \(P\text{CO}_2\) ([g] [PCO2]). [ICU] / [f] [MAP] / [g] [BRN] / [f] [QTc] / [f] [O₂] Hemodynamics, Burn & Emergency Keys Cardiac Output ([ICU]), MAP, Parkland Burn ([g] [BRN]) & Emergency Keys: Solves Q = H × S / 1000 ([Q], [H], [S]), mean arterial pressure \(\text{DBP} + (\text{SBP}-\text{DBP})/3\) ([f] [MAP]), Parkland burn fluid V = 4 × W × B ([V], [W], [B]), Bazett corrected \(\text{QTc}\) interval ([f] [QTc]), and oxygen tank duration ([f] [O₂]).

docs.title: Quantitative Finance, Actuarial Science, and Six Sigma Keycaps
docs.text:
On the SC-95 the Row 1 Time Value of Money workspace key ([TVM]), Row 1 and Row 2 R-style probability distribution keys, and shifted financial and statistical solvers combine five-variable compound interest, discounted cash-flow and bond valuation, unit-economic accounting, and Six Sigma statistical inference:

Keycap / Softkey Layer Operation & Stack Signature [TVM] \(\to\) [N] [I%] [PV] [PMT] [FV] [END]/[BEG] Row 1 Col 2 Primary & Softkeys Five-Variable TVM Workspace: Pressing [TVM] binds softkeys to [N], [I%], [PV], [PMT], [FV], and payment timing [END]/[BEG]; keying <VALUE> <SOFTKEY> stores a parameter (with 0 binding \(0.0000\)), [↰] <SOFTKEY> unbinds, and [g] [SOLVE] <SOFTKEY> (or [XEQ] <SOFTKEY>) solves for the unknown. [f] [BS] / [g] [CF] / [f] [EAR] Row 1 Col 2 (Yel/Blu) & Row 6 Col 1 Yel Black-Scholes Options ([f] [BS]), Cash Flows ([g] [CF]) & Effective Rate ([f] [EAR]): Evaluates European option pricing ([f] [BS]), opens discounted cash flows ([g] [CF]), or solves E = ((1 + A / (100 × M))^M - 1) × 100 ([E], [A], [M]) via [f] [EAR]. [g] [CAGR] / [g] [CAP] / [f] [CAPM] / [g] [DSCR] Capital Budgeting & Valuation Keys Compound annual growth rate ([g] [CAGR]), capitalization rate ([g] [CAP]), Capital Asset Pricing Model expected return ([f] [CAPM]), and debt service coverage ratio ([g] [DSCR]). [f] [MGN] / [f] [BEP] / [g] [EOQ] / [g] [DEP] / [g] [DDM] Commercial & Corporate Valuation Keys Gross margin M = (P - C) / P × 100 ([f] [MGN]), break-even production quantity Q = F / (P - V) ([f] [BEP]), economic order quantity Q = √(2×D×S/H) ([g] [EOQ]), straight-line depreciation D = (C - S) / L ([g] [DEP]), and Gordon dividend discount valuation ([g] [DDM]), while markup and sales tax are solved via [g] [EQN] MKP and [g] [EQN] TAX. [g] [BND] (Bond Valuation) Row 2 Col 1 Blue Shift Fixed-Income Bond Workspace ([g] [BND]): Solves P = C × (1 - (1 + Y/100)^-N) / (Y/100) + F / (1 + Y/100)^N forward for clean price [P] or backward for periodic yield to maturity [Y], coupon [C], remaining periods [N], or par redemption [F]. [g] [pN] / [f] [qN] / [rN] / [g] [pt] / [f] [qt] / [rt] / [g] [pχ²] / [f] [qχ²] / [rχ²] / [g] [pF] / [f] [qF] / [rF] / [g] [pB] / [f] [qB] / [rB] / [f] [PDF] Row 1 Col 3 & Row 2 Cols 2–5 R-Style CDF (p*), Inverse Quantile (q*), Random Variate (r*) & Density (PDF): Evaluates cumulative probabilities (blue shift), critical quantiles (yellow shift), and random variates (unshifted primary) for Binomial ([g] [pB]/[f] [qB]/[rB]), Normal ([g] [pN]/[f] [qN]/[rN]), Student's \(t\) ([g] [pt]/[f] [qt]/[rt]), Chi-square ([g] [pχ²]/[f] [qχ²]/[rχ²]), and Fisher \(F\) ([g] [pF]/[f] [qF]/[rF]) distributions, or prefixes with [f] [PDF] for point density/mass. [Σ+] / [f] [Σ-] / [x̄,ȳ] / [f] [MED] / [g] [s,σ] / [g] [L.R.] Summary Statistics & Regression Keys Accumulates/removes \((x_i, y_i)\) pairs ([Σ+], [f] [Σ-]), computes sample means ([x̄,ȳ]), median/IQR ([f] [MED]), sample/population standard deviations ([g] [s,σ]), and opens the least-squares regression menu ([g] [L.R.] \(\to\) [ŷ], [x̂], [m], [b], [r]). [g] [Cpk] / [g] [SPC] / [g] [CI] / [f] [z₀] / [f] [t₂] / [g] [A/B] / [f] [n*] / [g] [P B] / [g] [β] Six Sigma, Inference & Bayesian Solvers [%] / [f] [Δ%] / [g] [DDM] Row 7 Col 3 (Primary / Yellow / Blue) Percentage Functions & Equity Valuation: Standard percentage ([%]), percent change \(\Delta\%\) ([f] [Δ%]), and Gordon dividend discount equity valuation ([g] [DDM]). [f] [▸YR] / [g] [▸YMD] / [f] [DT+] / [g] [ΔD] Row 5 Cols 1–2 Shifted Keys Calendar & Day-Count Keys: Converts day counts to annualized years ([f] [▸YR]), toggles ISO YYYY.MMDD format ([g] [▸YMD]), projects calendar maturity dates ([f] [DT+]), and evaluates exact calendar days between dates ([g] [ΔD]). [f] [▸YR] / [g] [▸YMD] / [f] [DT+] / [g] [ΔD] Row 5 Cols 1–2 Shifted Keys Calendar & Day-Count Keys: Converts day counts to annualized years ([f] [▸YR]), toggles ISO YYYY.MMDD format ([g] [▸YMD]), projects calendar maturity dates ([f] [DT+]), and evaluates exact calendar days between dates ([g] [ΔD]).

docs.title: Appendix C: Solutions to Chapter Practice Problems
docs.text: This compendium provides complete step-by-step keystroke solutions, stack register traces, and intermediate mathematical verifications for all 135 practice problems across the 27 chapters of The Stack in the Field.

docs.title: Unit I (SC-35): Geomatics, Land Surveying & Flight Navigation
Chapter 1: The Lost Cornerstone in the Pine Barrens
docs.text:
1. Slope Reduction and Forward Coordinate Projection
  2. Keystrokes: 412.68 [ENTER] 6.15 [▸HR] [SLP] 47.2230 [▸HR] 410.10 [TRV] [f] [N⇄E]
  3. Solution: Reduces slope distance \(S = 412.68\text{ ft}\) at \(\nu = 6.25^\circ\) to horizontal distance \(D_H = \mathbf{410.10\text{ ft}}\) in \(X\) and vertical rise \(\Delta V = \mathbf{44.92\text{ ft}}\) in \(Y\). Staging azimuth \(47.375^\circ\) and \(D_H = 410.10\text{ ft}\) evaluates coordinate displacements \(\Delta N = \mathbf{277.75\text{ ft}}\) in \(Y\) and \(\Delta E = \mathbf{301.76\text{ ft}}\) in \(X\).
  4. Inverse Bearing Between Witness Monuments
  5. Keystrokes: 1585.20 [ENTER] 1200 [-] 1912.60 [ENTER] 1500 [-] [INV] [x⇄y] [BRG] [f] [▸HMS]
  6. Solution: Calculates coordinate differences \(\Delta N = 385.20\text{ ft}\) and \(\Delta E = 412.60\text{ ft}\) to yield boundary distance \(D = \mathbf{564.4624\text{ ft}}\), azimuth \(\alpha = \mathbf{46.9669^\circ}\), and legal quadrant bearing \(\mathbf{\text{N } 46^\circ 58' 01'' \text{ E}}\) (46.5801).
  7. Traverse Closure Precision and Acreage Conversion
  8. Keystrokes: 0.15 [ENTER] 0.20 [+/-] [g] [CLS] 2500 [x⇄y] [÷] 326700 [ENTER] 43560 [÷]
  9. Solution: Resolves linear error of closure \(E_c = \sqrt{0.15^2 + (-0.20)^2} = \mathbf{0.25\text{ ft}}\), computes relative precision ratio \(2500 / 0.25 = \mathbf{1 : 10{,}000}\), and converts \(326{,}700\text{ ft}^2\) to \(\mathbf{7.5000\text{ acres}}\).
  10. Architectural Foot-Inch Reduction and Colonial Chain Conversions
  11. Keystrokes: 38 [ENTER] 7 [ENTER] 5 [ENTER] 8 [÷] [+] 12 [÷] [+] 14.75 [ENTER] 66 [×]
  12. Solution: Evaluates fractional inches and feet to yield architectural offset \(L_{\text{ft}} = \mathbf{38.6354\text{ ft}}\), and multiplies \(14.75\text{ chains} \times 66\text{ ft/chain}\) to yield \(D = \mathbf{973.50\text{ ft}}\).
  13. State Plane Combined Grid-to-Ground Scale Reduction
  14. Keystrokes: 20906000 [ENTER] 20906000 [ENTER] 5280 [+] 30 [-] [÷] 0.9999450 [×] 3450 [×]
  15. Solution: Computes elevation factor \(k_{\text{elev}} = \mathbf{0.9997489}\), combined factor \(k_{\text{comb}} = \mathbf{0.9996940}\), and reduced State Plane grid distance \(D_{\text{grid}} = \mathbf{3{,}448.94\text{ ft}}\).

docs.title: Chapter 2: Threading the Switchback Grade Through Granite Gorge
docs.text:
1. Highway Curve Layout from Radius and Deflection Angle
  2. Keystrokes: 1200 [ENTER] 28.5 [CRV] 1200 [ENTER] 14.25 [SIN] [×] 2 [×]
  3. Solution: Evaluates curve parameters to place tangent distance \(T = \mathbf{304.77\text{ ft}}\) in \(Y\) and arc length \(L = \mathbf{596.90\text{ ft}}\) in \(X\), with long chord \(LC = 2R\sin(14.25^\circ) = \mathbf{590.80\text{ ft}}\).
  4. Parabolic Vertical Curve and Earthwork Cut Volume
  5. Keystrokes: 425.00 [ENTER] 2.5 [ENTER] 1.75 [+/-] [ENTER] 8 [f] [VCV] 250 [ENTER] 380 [ENTER] 180 [g] [CUT]
  6. Solution: Evaluates vertical curve equation to find midpoint elevation \(\text{Elev}(4) = \mathbf{430.75\text{ ft}}\), and computes average end-area cut volume \(V = \frac{250 + 380}{2} \times \frac{180}{27} = \mathbf{2{,}100.00\text{ yd}^3}\).
  7. Three-Wire Benchmark Transfer and Grade Check
  8. Keystrokes: 7.82 [ENTER] 5.42 [ENTER] 3.02 [f] [LVL] 842.15 [H] 5.32 [B] 5.42 [F] [g] [SOLVE] [E] 6 [+/-] [ENTER] 480 [g] [GR%]
  9. Solution: Confirms mid-wire \((7.82 + 3.02)/2 = \mathbf{5.42\text{ ft}}\) in \(Y\) and stadia distance \(D = 100 \times (7.82 - 3.02) = \mathbf{480.00\text{ ft}}\) in \(X\). Transferred elevation is \(E = \mathbf{842.05\text{ ft}}\) with grade \(\text{GR\%} = \mathbf{-1.2500\%}\).
  10. Highway Superelevation Rate and Side Friction Balance
  11. Keystrokes: 65 [f] [x²] 15 [ENTER] 1500 [×] [÷] 0.11 [-]
  12. Solution: Calculates total centrifugal demand \(e + f = 65^2 / (15 \times 1500) = \mathbf{0.1878\text{ ft/ft}}\), yielding required pavement superelevation \(e = 0.1878 - 0.110 = \mathbf{0.0778\text{ ft/ft}}\) (\(7.78\%\)).
  13. Prismoidal Earthwork Correction on Tapering Rock Cut
  14. Keystrokes: 820 [ENTER] 240 [ENTER] 200 [g] [CUT] 18 [ENTER] 8 [-] 64 [ENTER] 34 [-] [×] 200 [×] 324 [÷] [-]
  15. Solution: Evaluates Average End-Area volume \(V_{\text{ea}} = \mathbf{3{,}925.93\text{ yd}^3}\), prismoidal correction \(C_p = \frac{200}{324}(10)(30) = \mathbf{185.19\text{ yd}^3}\), and certified volume \(V_{\text{prism}} = 3925.93 - 185.19 = \mathbf{3{,}740.74\text{ yd}^3}\).

docs.title: Chapter 3: Night Approach Under a Mountain Crosswind
docs.text:
1. Wind Vector Decomposition and Crab Angle
  2. Keystrokes: 28 [ENTER] 40 [f] [WND] 145 [÷] [f] [ASIN]
  3. Solution: Resolves wind vector into headwind \(V_{\text{hw}} = \mathbf{21.45\text{ kt}}\) in \(Y\) and crosswind \(V_{\text{xw}} = \mathbf{18.00\text{ kt}}\) in \(X\). Dividing crosswind by airspeed yields crab angle \(\text{WCA} = \arcsin(18/145) = \mathbf{7.13^\circ}\).
  4. Inverse Wind Angle Limit and Density Altitude
  5. Keystrokes: 15 [X] 30 [V] [g] [SOLVE] [A] 6200 [ENTER] 28 [g] [ALT]
  6. Solution: Solves crosswind limit backward to find \(\theta_{\max} = \arcsin(15/30) = \mathbf{30.00^\circ}\). Evaluates atmospheric expansion to find Density Altitude \(\text{DA} = \mathbf{9{,}248\text{ ft}}\).
  7. Endurance Leg Check and Center of Gravity Moment
  8. Keystrokes: 165 [D] 1.25 [T] [g] [SOLVE] [S] 350 [ENTER] 120 [×]
  9. Solution: Solves time-speed-distance equation to yield required groundspeed \(S = 165 / 1.25 = \mathbf{132.00\text{ kt}}\), and computes fuel moment \(M = 350 \times 120 = \mathbf{42{,}000\text{ lb}\cdot\text{in}}\).
  10. Point of Equal Time on Headwind Route
  11. Keystrokes: 360 [ENTER] 170 [×] 130 [ENTER] 170 [+] [÷] 130 [÷]
  12. Solution: Evaluates Critical Point formula \(d_{\text{PET}} = \frac{D \times GS_{\text{ret}}}{GS_{\text{out}} + GS_{\text{ret}}} = \frac{360 \times 170}{300} = \mathbf{204.00\text{ NM}}\), requiring flight time \(t_{\text{PET}} = 204 / 130 = \mathbf{1.5692\text{ hr}}\) (\(94.15\text{ min}\)).
  13. High-Altitude Summer Takeoff Roll Expansion
  14. Keystrokes: 7000 [ENTER] 32 [g] [ALT] 1250 [ENTER] 10.720 [ENTER] 0.12 [×] 1 [+] [×]
  15. Solution: Calculates Density Altitude \(\text{DA} = \mathbf{10{,}720\text{ ft}}\). Evaluates takeoff expansion factor \(1 + (10.720 \times 0.12) = 2.2864\), yielding expanded ground roll \(S_{\text{ground}} = 1250 \times 2.2864 = \mathbf{2{,}858.00\text{ ft}}\).

docs.title: Unit II (SC-14): Electrical Power, Conduit Geometry & Industrial Trades
Chapter 4: The Voltage Drop on Pier 14's Crane Feeder
docs.text:
1. Three-Phase Line Current and Continuous Feeder Sizing
  2. Keystrokes: 480 [ENTER] 125 [g] [kVA] 1.25 [×]
  3. Solution: Calculates operating load current \(I = 125{,}000 / (\sqrt{3} \times 480) = \mathbf{150.3533\text{ A}}\), requiring minimum continuous feeder rating \(I_{\text{feeder}} = 1.25 \times 150.3533 = \mathbf{187.9416\text{ A}}\) (#3/0 AWG copper rated at \(200\text{ A}\)).
  4. Conductor Resistance and Three-Phase Voltage Drop
  5. Keystrokes: 480 [ENTER] 400 [ENTER] 160 [ENTER] 0.0766 [AWG]
  6. Solution: Evaluates three-phase voltage drop \(V_{\text{drop}} = \sqrt{3} \times 0.0766 \times 0.400 \times 160 = \mathbf{8.51\text{ V}}\) in \(Y\), percentage drop \(\mathbf{1.77\%}\) in \(X\), and delivered terminal voltage \(V_{\text{load}} = \mathbf{471.49\text{ V}}\) in \(Z\).
  7. Power Factor Correction Capacitor Sizing
  8. Keystrokes: 120 [ENTER] 0.75 [PF] 0.75 [f] [ACOS] [TAN] 0.95 [f] [ACOS] [TAN] [-] 120 [×]
  9. Solution: Evaluates uncorrected reactive load \(Q_1 = 120 \times \tan(41.41^\circ) = \mathbf{105.8301\text{ kVAR}}\). Computes required capacitance \(Q_C = 120(\tan 41.41^\circ - \tan 18.19^\circ) = \mathbf{66.4027\text{ kVAR}}\).
  10. Three-Phase Motor Inrush and Branch Fuse Sizing
  11. Keystrokes: 124 [ENTER] 1.25 [×] 124 [ENTER] 1.75 [×]
  12. Solution: Computes minimum conductor ampacity \(1.25 \times 124 = \mathbf{155.00\text{ A}}\), and evaluates maximum fuse threshold \(1.75 \times 124 = \mathbf{217.00\text{ A}}\) (selecting standard \(225\text{ A}\) time-delay fuses).
  13. Substation Available Short-Circuit Fault Current
  14. Keystrokes: 1500000 [ENTER] 480 [÷] 3 [√x] [÷] 0.0575 [÷]
  15. Solution: Evaluates rated secondary current \(I_{\text{FLA}} = 1{,}500{,}000 / (\sqrt{3} \times 480) = \mathbf{1{,}804.22\text{ A}}\), and computes short-circuit current \(I_{\text{sc}} = 1804.22 / 0.0575 = \mathbf{31{,}377.73\text{ A}}\) (requiring \(35\text{ kA}\) or \(65\text{ kA}\) rated switchgear).

docs.title: Chapter 5: Bending Four Conduits Around the Boiler-Room I-Beam
docs.text:
1. Conduit Offset Travel and Shrinkage Deduction
  2. Keystrokes: 9.5 [ENTER] 30 [OFS]
  3. Solution: Evaluates offset geometry to place travel distance \(T = 9.5 / \sin(30^\circ) = \mathbf{19.00\text{ in.}}\) in \(X\) and conduit shrinkage deduction \(S = 9.5 \times (1/\sin 30^\circ - 1/\tan 30^\circ) = \mathbf{2.55\text{ in.}}\) in \(Y\).
  4. Compound Rolling Offset Spatial Travel
  5. Keystrokes: 14 [ENTER] 18 [ENTER] 45 [OFS]
  6. Solution: Resolves spatial hypotenuse \(D_{\text{spatial}} = \sqrt{14^2 + 18^2} = \mathbf{22.80\text{ in.}}\), yielding travel distance \(T = 22.8035 \times \sqrt{2} = \mathbf{32.25\text{ in.}}\) in \(X\) and shrinkage \(S = \mathbf{9.45\text{ in.}}\) in \(Y\).
  7. Three-Point Saddle Mark Layout and Shrink
  8. Keystrokes: 4 [ENTER] 45 [g] [FIT]
  9. Solution: Calculates outer mark distance from center \(D = 4.0 \times 2.613 = \mathbf{10.00\text{ in.}}\) in \(X\) and total conduit shrinkage deduction \(S = 4.0 \times \frac{3}{16} = \mathbf{1.88\text{ in.}}\) in \(Y\).
  10. Four-Bend Saddle Over Rectangular Duct
  11. Keystrokes: 6 [ENTER] 30 [OFS] 2 [×] 16 [ENTER] 1.608 [+]
  12. Solution: Evaluates individual travel \(T = \mathbf{12.00\text{ in.}}\) and shrinkage \(S = \mathbf{1.61\text{ in.}}\) per offset. Total conduit length shrinkage across both offsets is \(\mathbf{3.22\text{ in.}}\), with inside mark spacing \(16.0 + 1.61 = \mathbf{17.61\text{ in.}}\).
  13. NEC Conduit Fill and Conductor Ampacity Derating
  14. Keystrokes: 0.864 [ENTER] 0.40 [×] 30 [ENTER] 0.70 [×]
  15. Solution: Computes maximum allowable conductor fill area \(0.864 \times 0.40 = \mathbf{0.3456\text{ in.}^2}\), and evaluates derated continuous conductor ampacity \(30 \times 0.70 = \mathbf{21.00\text{ A}}\).

docs.title: Chapter 6: The Chattering Milling Cutter and the Drifting Pressure Loop
docs.text:
1. Milling Spindle Speed and Table Feed Rate
  2. Keystrokes: 350 [ENTER] 3 [f] [SFM] 0.006 [ENTER] 5 [×] [×]
  3. Solution: Evaluates spindle rotation speed \(N = \frac{350 \times 3.8197}{3.0} = \mathbf{445.63\text{ RPM}}\) in \(X\). Multiplying by chip load and 5 flutes yields table feed rate \(F = 445.63 \times 0.006 \times 5 = \mathbf{13.37\text{ in./min}}\) in \(X\).
  4. Twelve-Hole Flange Bolt Circle and Inverse Cutter Diameter
  5. Keystrokes: 10.5 [ENTER] 12 [g] [BC] 400 [ENTER] 1200 [f] [SFM]
  6. Solution: Evaluates bolt circle chord length \(C = 10.5 \times \sin(15^\circ) = \mathbf{2.7176\text{ in.}}\) in \(X\). Solves cutting speed equation backward to yield maximum allowable cutter diameter \(D = \frac{400 \times 3.8197}{1200} = \mathbf{1.2732\text{ in.}}\).
  7. Process Loop Calibration and Inverse Valve Sizing
  8. Keystrokes: 175 [ENTER] 250 [mA] 85 [ENTER] 12 [g] [Cᵥ]
  9. Solution: Scales analog instrumentation loop to return output current \(I = 4 + (16 \times 175/250) = \mathbf{15.20\text{ mA}}\) in \(X\). Calculates required valve sizing coefficient \(C_v = 85 / \sqrt{12} = \mathbf{24.5374}\) in \(X\).
  10. CNC Milling Stability Pocket and Feed Acceleration
  11. Keystrokes: 800 [ENTER] 0.5 [f] [SFM] 0.0035 [ENTER] 3 [×] [×]
  12. Solution: Evaluates spindle rotation speed \(N = \frac{800 \times 3.8197}{0.5} = \mathbf{6{,}111.55\text{ RPM}}\), yielding programmed table feed rate \(F = 6111.55 \times 0.0035 \times 3 = \mathbf{64.17\text{ in./min}}\).
  13. Hydraulic Oil Valve Sizing and Pressure Inversion
  14. Keystrokes: 140 [ENTER] 32 [ENTER] 0.88 [g] [Cᵥ]

docs.title: Unit III (SC-16): Digital Systems, Bitwise Logic & Embedded Timing
Chapter 7: The Stuck Interrupt Flag in the Motor Controller
docs.text:
1. Two's Complement Additive Inversion
  2. Keystrokes: [f] [DEC] 8 [g] [WSZ] 42 [f] [NEG] [HEX] 42 [f] [DEC] [+]
  3. Solution: Sets 8-bit word size and negates to yield \(-42_{10} = \mathbf{\text{0xD6}}\) in \(X\). Adding \(+42\) produces modular overflow to \(\mathbf{\text{0x00}}\), confirming the two's complement additive inverse.
  4. Contiguous Bitmask Generation
  5. Keystrokes: [HEX] 16 [g] [WSZ] 6 [ENTER] 9 [f] [MSK]
  6. Solution: Generates a 6-bit contiguous mask shifted left by 9 bit positions to return \((2^6 - 1) \ll 9 = 63 \ll 9 = \mathbf{\text{0x7E00}}\) in \(X\).
  7. Logical vs. Arithmetic Right Shift
  8. Keystrokes: [HEX] 16 [g] [WSZ] C000 [ENTER] 3 [≫] [f] [DEC] C000 [HEX] 3 [f] [ASR] [f] [DEC]
  9. Solution: Logical right shift shifts in zero bits, returning \(\mathbf{8{,}192}\) (0x1800, corrupting the sign). Arithmetic right shift replicates the sign bit, returning exactly \(\mathbf{-2{,}048}\) (0xF800, \(-16{,}384 / 8 = -2{,}048\)).
  10. Cortex-M Bit-Band Alias Address Calculation
  11. Keystrokes: [HEX] 32 [g] [WSZ] 40020014 [ENTER] 40000000 [-] 32 [f] [DEC] [×] 3 [ENTER] 4 [×] [+] 42000000 [HEX] [+]
  12. Solution: Calculates byte offset 0x20014 (\(131{,}092_{10}\)), multiplies by 32, adds bit word offset \(3 \times 4 = 12\), and adds alias base 0x42000000 to yield alias address \(\mathbf{\text{0x4240028C}}\).
  13. Q8.8 Fixed-Point Voltage Threshold Encoding
  14. Keystrokes: [f] [DEC] 16 [g] [WSZ] 3.625 [ENTER] 256 [×] [HEX]
  15. Solution: Multiplies floating-point voltage by scaling factor \(2^8 = 256\) to yield \(3.625 \times 256 = 928_{10} = \mathbf{\text{0x03A0}}\) in \(X\) (integer part 0x03 = \(3\text{ V}\), fraction 0xA0/256 = \(0.625\text{ V}\)).

docs.title: Chapter 8: The Corrupt Sensor Packet Across the Serial Bus
docs.text:
1. IEEE-754 Single-Precision Float Encoding
  2. Keystrokes: [f] [DEC] 12.5 [f] [NEG] [FLT]
  3. Solution: Decomposes \(-12.50 = -1.1001_2 \times 2^3\) into sign \(s=1\), biased exponent \(e = 3 + 127 = 130\) (0x82), and mantissa fraction 0x480000 to assemble binary word \(\mathbf{\text{0xC1480000}}\) in \(X\).
  4. 32-Bit Endianness Reversal
  5. Keystrokes: [HEX] 32 [g] [WSZ] 00409642 [g] [SWP]
  6. Solution: Executes 32-bit byte reversal, transposing byte sequence \([B_0, B_1, B_2, B_3] \to [B_3, B_2, B_1, B_0]\) to return \(\mathbf{\text{0x42964000}}\) (\(+75.125^\circ\text{C}\) in IEEE-754).
  7. CIDR /28 Subnet Sizing
  8. Keystrokes: [HEX] 32 [g] [WSZ] FFFFFFFF [ENTER] 4 [≪] [f] [DEC] 2 [ENTER] 4 [f] [yˣ] 2 [-]
  9. Solution: Shifts 32 ones left by \(32 - 28 = 4\) bits to yield subnet mask \(\mathbf{\text{0xFFFFFFF0}}\) (255.255.255.240). Total block is \(2^4 = 16\) IPs, yielding \(16 - 2 = \mathbf{14\text{ usable hosts}}\).
  10. 16x Oversampled UART Baud Divisor on an 80 MHz Clock
  11. Keystrokes: 80000000 [ENTER] 16 [ENTER] 921600 [×] [÷] 5 [ENTER] 16 [×] 80000000 [x⇄y] [÷] 921600 [-] 921600 [÷] 100 [×]
  12. Solution: Calculates ideal divisor \(\text{BRR} = 80\times 10^6 / (16 \times 921{,}600) = \mathbf{5.4253}\). Rounding to integer divisor 5 yields actual baud \(1{,}000{,}000\text{ bps}\), producing an intolerable error of \(\mathbf{+8.51\%}\).
  13. Reflected CRC-32 Verification of a 4-Byte Payload
  14. Keystrokes: [HEX] 32 [g] [WSZ] 12345678 [ENTER] 32 [f] [CRC]
  15. Solution: Executes reflected polynomial division over Galois Field \(GF(2)\) using generator polynomial 0xEDB88320, returning standard Ethernet/ZIP frame check sequence \(\mathbf{\text{0xDF8A8A2B}}\).

  2. Keystrokes: 2.5 [ENTER] 65536 [÷] 1000000 [×] 35904 [ENTER] 2.5 [×] 65536 [÷]
  3. Solution: Calculates quantization step resolution \(V_{\text{LSB}} = 2.50 / 65536 = \mathbf{38.147\ \mu\text{V}}\) in \(X\). Reconstructing analog input voltage yields \(V_{\text{in}} = (35{,}904 / 65536) \times 2.50 = \mathbf{1.36975\text{ V}}\).

  5. Keystrokes: 32 [ENTER] 22 [-] 2 [x⇄y] [f] [yˣ] 2 [-]
  6. Solution: Calculates host address space \(2^{32-22} = 2^{10} = \mathbf{1{,}024\text{ IPs}}\), yielding \(1024 - 2 = \mathbf{1{,}022\text{ usable hosts}}\). Broadcast address is \(\mathbf{10.240.19.255}\) (0x0AF013FF).
  7. Cache-Line Descriptor Alignment and Power-of-Two Ring Sizing
  8. Keystrokes: 128 [ENTER] 48 [×] 64 [ENTER] 6144 [x⇄y] [÷]
  9. Solution: Calculates total raw buffer footprint \(128 \times 48 = \mathbf{6{,}144\text{ bytes}}\). Because \(6144 / 64 = 96.00\) divides evenly, zero padding bytes are required, aligning naturally to cache-line boundaries.
  10. High-Speed Synchronous SPI Bus Setup Timing Margin
  11. Keystrokes: 20 [ENTER] 12 [-] 2.5 [-] 6 [-]
  12. Solution: Calculates remaining setup slack margin \(T_{\text{slack}} = 20.0 - (12.0 + 2.5 + 6.0) = 20.0 - 20.5 = \mathbf{-0.50\text{ ns}}\), revealing a severe timing violation requiring a reduced bus clock.
  13. PWM Ultrasonic Auto-Reload Period Sizing
  14. Keystrokes: 120000000 [ENTER] 2 [ENTER] 20000 [×] [÷]
  15. Solution: In center-aligned mode, the timer counts up and down, requiring period count \(\text{ARR} = f_{\text{TIM}} / (2 \times f_{\text{PWM}}) = 120\times 10^6 / 40{,}000 = \mathbf{3{,}000}\) (0x0BB8).

docs.title: Unit IV (SC-24): Cinema, Broadcast Engineering & Concert Production

  7. High-Speed Phantom Overcrank at 240 fps in the Timecode Solver

At 15 elapsed minutes, skipping 2 frame numbers per minute except on tens gives \(N_{\text{dropped}} = 2(15 - \lfloor 15/10 \rfloor) = 2(15 - 1) = \mathbf{28\text{ dropped labels}}\).

docs.title: Chapter 11: Holding Focus on the Steadicam Close-Up at Dusk

1. Super 35 Portrait Prime Field of View and Hyperfocal Distance
  2. Keystrokes: 24.89 [ENTER] 85 [FOV] 85 [ENTER] 4 [ENTER] 0.025 [DOF]
  3. Solution: Computes horizontal field of view \(A = 2\arctan(24.89 / (2 \times 85)) = \mathbf{16.659^\circ}\). Evaluates hyperfocal distance \(H = F^2 / (N \times C) = 85^2 / (4 \times 0.025) = 72{,}250\text{ mm} = \mathbf{72.25\text{ m}}\).
  4. European 25 fps Exterior Exposure and 5-Stop ND Filter
  5. Keystrokes: 25 [ENTER] 180 [f] [SHT] 11 [ENTER] 0.02 [EV] 5 [g] [▸ND]
  6. Solution: Computes scene exposure \(E = \log_2(11^2 / 0.02) = \mathbf{12.563\text{ EV}}\). Opening \(5\text{ stops}\) requires neutral density optical density \(D = 5 \times 0.3 = \mathbf{1.5}\) in \(X\) and light reduction filter factor \(2^5 = \mathbf{32\times}\) in \(Y\).
  7. Follow-Spot Illuminance and Daylight-to-Tungsten Mired Shift
  8. Keystrokes: 48000 [ENTER] 12 [f] [x²] [÷] [f] [▸fc] 5600 [ENTER] 3200 [g] [GEL]
  9. Solution: Evaluates inverse-square illuminance \(E_{\text{lx}} = 48{,}000 / 144 = \mathbf{333.333\text{ lx}}\) and converts to \(E_{\text{fc}} = \mathbf{30.968\text{ fc}}\). Mired shift \(\Delta M = 10^6(1/3200 - 1/5600) = \mathbf{+133.93\text{ Mireds}}\) (Full CTO).
  10. Anamorphic 2.0x Squeeze Field of View and Full-Frame Matching
  11. Keystrokes: 49.78 [ENTER] 40 [FOV] 63.785 [A] 36 [W] [XEQ] [F]

  13. Micro-Reciprocal Degree Gel Stacking and Resulting Color Temperature
  14. Keystrokes: 6000 [f] [▸MRD] 137 [+] 68 [+] 1000000 [x⇄y] [÷]

docs.title: Chapter 12: Aligning the Stadium Delay Towers Before Downbeat

  5. Keystrokes: 92 [ENTER] 90 [dB] 94 [dB] 2 [ENTER] 32 [f] [SPL]
  6. Solution: Incoherent decibel summation yields stage level \(L_{\Sigma} = \mathbf{96.83\text{ dBSPL}}\). Spherical inverse-square attenuation over distance ratio \(32/2 = 16\times\) (\(20\log_{10}(16) = 24.08\text{ dB}\)) reduces front-of-house level to \(L_{\text{FOH}} = \mathbf{72.75\text{ dBSPL}}\).
  7. Broadcast Line-Level Voltage and Maximum PA Throw Distance
  8. Keystrokes: 18 [g] [▸V] 138 [ENTER] 102 [-] 20 [÷] 10 [x⇄y] [f] [yˣ]
  9. Solution: Converts \(+18.0\text{ dBu}\) to line voltage \(V_{\text{rms}} = 0.7746 \times 10^{18/20} = \mathbf{6.153\text{ V}_{\text{rms}}}\). Allowable free-field attenuation is \(138 - 102 = 36\text{ dB}\), yielding maximum throw distance \(D = 10^{36/20} = \mathbf{63.10\text{ m}}\).
  10. Architectural Reverberation Sizing via Sabine's Formula
  11. Keystrokes: 0.161 [ENTER] 1800 [×] 217.6 [÷] 0.161 [ENTER] 1800 [×] 0.85 [÷] 217.6 [-]
  12. Solution: Sabine's formula evaluates untreated room reverberation \(RT_{60} = 0.161(1800) / 217.6 = \mathbf{1.332\text{ s}}\). Reaching target \(0.85\text{ s}\) requires total absorption \(340.94\text{ sabins}\), demanding an additional \(\Delta A = \mathbf{123.34\text{ m}^2\text{-sabins}}\).
  13. Axial Room Mode Resonances and Comb Filtering
  14. Keystrokes: 343 [ENTER] 2 [ENTER] 4.25 [×] [÷] 2 [×] 3 [×] 1 [ENTER] 2 [ENTER] 0.00245 [×] [÷]
  15. Solution: Axial modes resonate at \(f_1 = \mathbf{40.35\text{ Hz}}\), \(f_2 = \mathbf{80.71\text{ Hz}}\), and \(f_3 = \mathbf{121.06\text{ Hz}}\). Reflection delay \(\Delta t = 2.45\text{ ms}\) creates its first destructive cancellation notch at \(f_{\text{null}} = 1/(2 \times 0.00245) = \mathbf{204.08\text{ Hz}}\).

docs.title: Chapter 14: Clearing the Ridge on a Twelve-Kilometer Microwave Backhaul

docs.title: Chapter 15: Isolating the Mixer Spurious Products on the Tracking Generator

  2. Keystrokes: 1.2 10 [÷] [f] [10ˣ] 2 10 [÷] [f] [10ˣ] 1 [-] 20 10 [÷] [f] [10ˣ] [÷] [+] 6 10 [÷] [f] [10ˣ] 1 [-] 18 10 [÷] [f] [10ˣ] [÷] [+] [f] [LOG] 10 [×] 30 [ENTER] -174 [ENTER] 1.23 [+] 40 [+] [-] 2 [×] 3 [÷]

Noise floor in \(10\text{ kHz}\) is \(P_{\text{noise}} = -174 + 1.23 + 40 = -132.77\text{ dBm}\). Evaluating dynamic range yields \(\text{SFDR} = \frac{2}{3}(OIP_3 - P_{\text{noise}}) = \frac{2}{3}(30 - (-132.77)) = \mathbf{108.51\text{ dB}}\).
  4. Wireless Local Loop Shannon Channel Capacity

docs.title: Unit VI (SC-60): Analytical Chemistry & Laboratory Sciences

  12. Solution: Single stage error is \(\sigma_{\text{stage}} = \sqrt{1.2^2 + 0.4^2} = \mathbf{1.265\%}\). Propagating across four uncorrelated serial stages gives total analytical uncertainty \(\sigma_{\text{total}} = \sqrt{4} \times 1.265\% = \mathbf{2.530\%}\).
  13. Cryoscopic Freezing Point Depression of Saline
  14. Keystrokes: 9 [ENTER] 58.443 [÷] 1.86 [×] 1.858 [×] [+/-]
  15. Solution: Osmolality is \(\xi = m \times i = 0.1540 \times 1.860 = \mathbf{0.2864\text{ Osm/kg}}\) (\(286.4\text{ mOsm/kg}\)). Freezing point depression is \(\Delta T_f = K_f \times \xi = 1.858 \times 0.2864 = 0.5322^\circ\text{C}\), yielding freezing point \(T_f = \mathbf{-0.5322^\circ\text{C}}\).

docs.title: Chapter 17: Holding pH 7.40 Against an Acid Spike
docs.text:
1. Hydronium Ion Concentration and Autoionization
  2. Keystrokes: 7.382 [+/-] 10 [x⇄y] [f] [yˣ] 1000000000 [×] 1 [ENTER] 14 [+/-] 10ˣ 4.15 [ENTER] 9 [+/-] 10ˣ [÷]
  3. Solution: Hydronium ion concentration is \([\text{H}_3\text{O}^+] = 10^{-7.382} = 4.150 \times 10^{-8}\text{ M} = \mathbf{41.50\text{ nM}}\). Hydroxide ion concentration is \([\text{OH}^-] = K_w / [\text{H}_3\text{O}^+] = \mathbf{2.410 \times 10^{-7}\text{ M}}\) (\(241.0\text{ nM}\)).
  4. Acetate Buffer Ratio and pH Shift
  5. Keystrokes: 0.1 [ENTER] 0.05 [÷] [LOG] 4.756 [+] 0.09 [ENTER] 0.06 [÷] [LOG] 4.756 [+]
  6. Solution: Initial Henderson–Hasselbalch pH is \(\text{pH} = 4.756 + \log_{10}(2.0) = \mathbf{5.057}\). After adding \(0.010\text{ M}\) acid, \([\text{A}^-] = 0.090\) and \([\text{HA}] = 0.060\), shifting pH to \(4.756 + \log_{10}(1.5) = \mathbf{4.932}\) (a buffering shift of only \(\mathbf{-0.125\text{ pH units}}\)).
  7. Van Slyke Maximum Buffer Capacity
  8. Keystrokes: 2.3026 [ENTER] 0.08 [×] 0.25 [×] 2.3026 [ENTER] 0.08 [×] 0.9091 [×] 0.0909 [×]
  9. Solution: Maximum buffer capacity at \(\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a\) is \(\beta_{\max} = 0.5756 \times C = \mathbf{0.04605\text{ M/pH}}\) (\(46.05\text{ mM/pH}\)). At \(\text{pH} = 8.550\) (\(\alpha_1 = 0.9091, \alpha_0 = 0.0909\)), capacity drops to \(\beta = \mathbf{0.01522\text{ M/pH}}\) (\(15.22\text{ mM/pH}\))—a \(67\%\) loss in protective buffering capacity.
  10. Volumetric Standardization of Hydrochloric Acid
  11. Keystrokes: 0.105 [ENTER] 28.45 [×] 25 [÷]
  12. Solution: Equivalence stoichiometry yields acid molarity \(C_{\text{HCl}} = (C_{\text{titrant}} \times V_{\text{eq}}) / V_{\text{sample}} = (0.1050 \times 28.45) / 25.00 = \mathbf{0.1195\text{ M}}\).
  13. Diprotic Carbonic Acid Blood Buffer Shift
  14. Keystrokes: 24 [ENTER] 1.2 [÷] [LOG] 6.1 [+] 24 [ENTER] 2.4 [÷] [LOG] 6.1 [+]
  15. Solution: Normal arterial pH is \(\text{pH} = 6.100 + \log_{10}(24.0 / 1.20) = 6.100 + 1.301 = \mathbf{7.401}\). Acute doubling of dissolved carbon dioxide acid drops pH to \(6.100 + \log_{10}(10.0) = \mathbf{7.100}\)—inducing severe, life-threatening uncompensated respiratory acidosis.

  8. Keystrokes: 2000 [ENTER] 1.1182 [ENTER] 5 [+/-] 10ˣ [×] 16.5 [×] [÷] [√x]

  11. Keystrokes: 0.01 [LOG] 0.05916 [×] 2 [÷] 1.1 [x⇄y] [-]

  14. Keystrokes: 15500 [+/-] 8.31446 [÷] 310.15 [÷] [+/-] [eˣ]

docs.title: Prologue: Writing Equations for Space, Solving Them in Time
docs.text:
In the autumn of 1924, in a quiet lecture hall at the University of Warsaw, the Polish logician and philosopher Jan Łukasiewicz stood before a blackboard covered in logic formulas and examined a curious habit of mathematical notation (Łukasiewicz, 1924): the ubiquity of parentheses.

Every high-school student who has ever stared at a page of Algebra II or Precalculus knows the feeling of parenthesis vertigo. You look at an equation on a printed page:

\[x = \sqrt{7 + \sqrt{13 + \sqrt{29 + \sqrt{41}}}} \tag{Eq. 0.1}\]

or a compound rational fraction from physics or chemistry:

\[Q = \frac{12.4 \times 8.6}{3.2 + 4.9} \tag{Eq. 0.2}\]

On paper, your eyes naturally read from left to right and from the outside in. In this radical pyramid, the first symbol you encounter on the left is the outer square-root radical \(\sqrt{\dots}\), followed by \(7 +\), followed by a second radical, a third radical, and finally, at the far right end of the line, the number \(41\).

The moment you sit down to solve that equation, the outer square root cannot be evaluated first because you cannot take the square root of a sum that has not been added yet. To find \(x\), evaluation must ignore the left-to-right order of the ink and travel straight to the innermost number, \(41\), extracting its square root first, adding \(29\), taking the next square root, adding \(13\), extracting that root, and finally adding \(7\) before one last square root completes the chain from right to left.

This mismatch—between equations printed from the outside in and calculations evaluated by every human mind and computer processor from the inside out—is a historical artifact of the printing press.

docs.title: The Typesetter's Bargain and the Inside-Out Mind
docs.text:
For thousands of years, from Babylonian clay scribes and Greek geometers to medieval Arab algebraists, mathematics was written out in spoken sentences: "Take forty-one, extract its root, add twenty-nine to what results..." Spoken language unfolds in time. Physical measurement and instrumentation follow the same chronological order, staging inputs first and triggering the operation second: an electrical engineer connects two test probes to an oscilloscope before triggering a differential sweep, and a chemist weighs two reagents on a balance before combining them in a beaker. In speech, measurement, and calculation alike, an operation cannot occur until its operands exist.

In the sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries, however, Renaissance mathematicians and European printers faced an economic problem. Movable lead type was expensive, and rag paper was costly. Printers wanted to pack an entire finished mathematical thought onto a single static horizontal line of type. To fit a multi-step timeline onto a flat two-dimensional line, they wedged action symbols (+, -, ×, ÷) between numbers in a convention called infix notation, and invented parentheses ( ), brackets [ ], and horizontal fraction bars as punctuation fences to warn the eye: "Do not read this line from left to right; jump inside the deepest fence first."

That 16th-century typesetter's bargain was well suited to static paper, where the eye can scan back and forth across a page. It became a cognitive obstacle the moment 20th-century engineers copied paper notation onto electronic calculator keyboards.

When you type an infix string like ( ( 12.4 × 8.6 ) ÷ ( 3.2 + 4.9 ) ) = into an algebraic pocket or smartphone calculator, you must feed the machine in the sequence of the printed ink, reversing the natural order of evaluation. Halfway through the formula, when you press ÷ (, the calculation stalls because the denominator (3.2 + 4.9) does not yet exist. Because human working memory holds only about four active items at once (Miller, 1956; Sweller, 1988), hiding intermediate numbers behind a single-line display while counting nested parentheses ( ( ... ) / ( ... ) ) diverts attention from the physical structure of the problem to clerical punctuation (Strogatz, 2012; Strogatz, 2019; Ellenberg, 2014).

docs.title: Jan Łukasiewicz's Breakthrough and the Four Visible Registers
docs.text:
In 1924, Jan Łukasiewicz proved a simple theorem (Łukasiewicz, 1924): if operators are placed consistently before or after their operands, parentheses disappear from mathematical notation. No matter how deeply an equation is nested, the order in which numbers combine is unambiguous without a single bracket or precedence rule.

Three decades later, Australian philosopher and computer scientist Charles Hamblin (1957) (Hamblin, 1957) paired the postfix (Reverse Polish) form of Łukasiewicz's parenthesis-free notation, in which operands precede their operator, with a last-in, first-out hardware memory structure: an operational stack.

On a four-register operational stack, four horizontal display lines are arranged from bottom to top as Registers \(X, Y, Z,\) and \(T\). Register \(X\) at the bottom of the screen is the active register where keyed digits appear and where every unary or binary operation writes its immediate result. When a first operand is completed in Register \(X\) and the central ENTER bar is pressed, that value copies upward into Register \(Y\), preparing Register \(X\) to receive the second operand. Whenever a calculation spans two or three separate branches—like the numerator and denominator of a rational expression—the completed subtotal from the first branch lifts into Register \(Z\) (and Register \(T\)) to remain visible while the second branch is evaluated across Registers \(Y\) and \(X\). As soon as that second branch reduces to a single value in Register \(X\), the waiting subtotal in Register \(Z\) drops back into Register \(Y\) so the two operands align for the final binary operation.

When equations are read from their innermost operands outward, expressions from disparate branches of science reveal shared algebraic skeletons (Horowitz & Hill, 2015). Wiring electrical resistors in parallel, focusing light through a thin optical lens, and averaging a round-trip velocity all follow the binary harmonic relation \(x \parallel y = (x^{-1} + y^{-1})^{-1}\), while nested expressions unfold in two-register steps from the deepest term out. In the four-level radical \(x = \sqrt{7 + \sqrt{13 + \sqrt{29 + \sqrt{41}}}}\), evaluation starts at the radicand \(41\): extracting \(\sqrt{41} \approx 6.403\) inside Register \(X\), adding \(29\) and taking the square root (\(\approx 5.95\)), and adding \(13\) and taking the square root (\(\approx 4.353\)) leaves one final addition of \(7\) and square root to yield \(x \approx \mathbf{3.369}\), while Registers \(Z\) and \(T\) remain at zero.

docs.title: From Warsaw to the Shirt Pocket: The Four-Register Lineage
docs.text:
Łukasiewicz's 1924 logic notation and Hamblin's 1957 hardware stack, formalized for digital computer evaluation by Arthur Burks, Don Warren, and Jesse Wright in 1954 (Burks et al., 1954), became the native operating language of scientific instruments through the engineering work of Hewlett-Packard in Palo Alto and Corvallis. Following Thomas Osborne's floating-point prototype and the desktop HP 9100A in 1968, William R. Hewlett challenged Osborne, David S. Cochran, and Thomas M. Whitney in 1971 to condense trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential computation into a shirt-pocket instrument. Their work produced the 35-key HP-35 in January 1972 (Whitney, Rodé & Tung, 1972; Cochran, 1972), which replaced the slide rule with a four-register operational stack (\(X, Y, Z, T\)).

Over the next two decades, Hewlett-Packard's Corvallis Division and UC Berkeley numerical analyst William M. Kahan steadily expanded that four-register architecture (Hamrick, 1996). The HP-65 (1974) and HP-41C (1979) introduced magnetic program storage, alphanumeric displays, and an international community of engineers who shared algorithms through Richard J. Nelson's PPC Journal (Nelson, 1974; Musch, Wong & Conklin, 1980). Between 1979 and 1982, Kahan and the Corvallis engineering team led by Eric A. Evett, Paul J. McClellan, and Joseph P. Tanzini brought Richard Brent's hybrid root-finding algorithm (SOLVE), adaptive Romberg quadrature (∫), and split-stack complex arithmetic (CMPLX) into the HP-34C (1979) and the horizontal Voyager series—the HP-15C scientific, HP-12C financial, and HP-16C computer-scientist instruments (Kahan, 1979; HP, 1982; Evett et al., 1983).

In 1988 and 1991, the portrait-oriented Pioneer series—the HP-32S and HP-32SII (HP, 1991)—united one-handed vertical ergonomics with 26 named A–Z variables, a symbolic Equation List (EQN), mixed-fraction display, contextual function menus (PARTS, PROB, L.R., SUM, BASE, FLAGS), and metric–imperial unit conversions on the digit keys.

docs.title: Standing on the Shoulders of the HP-32SII and the RPN Tradition
docs.text: The StackCalc SC-32 continues the HP-32SII architecture and this four-decade lineage of parenthesis-free scientific instruments (Whitney, Rodé & Tung, 1972; Cochran, 1972; Kahan, 1979; HP, 1982; Evett et al., 1983; HP, 1991). Honoring the keyboard grammar, stack-lift rules, and numerical algorithms pioneered by Cochran, Kahan, and the Corvallis engineers, the SC-32 places all four stack registers (\(T, Z, Y, X\)) in full view on a 4-line transflective LCD above a dedicated 6-key dynamic softkey strip, while preserving the tactile one-handed portrait layout and four-register invariants (4-LVL, 8-LVL, and INF via FLAGS).
